source.$schema_note: 12 NYCRR fee schedule provisions: Subpart 329-1 (Medical Fee Schedule) in full, and the sections carrying the 14 January 2026 proposed amendment (329-1.3, 329-4.2, 333.2, 343.2, 348.2) with their applicability siblings (329-4.1, 333.1, 343.1, 348.1). source.decomposition_note: IN: 329-1.1, 329-1.2, 329-1.3 (a) to (e); 329-4.1, 329-4.2; 333.1, 333.2; 343.1, 343.2; 348.1, 348.2. OUT, named rather than dropped: Subpart 329-2 (ambulatory surgery, APG methodology) and Subpart 329-3 (emergency room, hospital clinics) are fee schedule provisions but are not on the January 2026 amendment's path, and 329-2.1(b) carries CPT codes with descriptors and a dollar table in the regulation text itself, which the licensing non-goal excludes from reproduction. 12 NYCRR 325-1.8 (telemedicine), referenced by 329-4.2(d), 333.2(c) and 348.2(c), is public and retrievable and is outside scope; whether an encounter qualifies under it arrives as a supplied fact. WCL 13-g (arbitration committee) and Education Law 6738(a) are statute, not this instrument.

entries.question: For a physical therapy or occupational therapy service, which schedule governs: the medical fee schedule (329-1.1) or the physical therapy and occupational therapy fee schedule (329-4.1(b))?

competing_readings.basis: 329-1.1 names `medical, physical therapy and occupational therapy services` and `the medical fee schedule`, and has not been amended since its 2015 renumbering.

329-4.1(b), adopted 2019 effective 2020-01-01, is the later and the specific provision, and 329-4.2(b) incorporates a schedule whose title names physical and occupational therapy. The Board's 2026 proposal moves PTA/OTA coding to that schedule, which reads as the Board's own view.

entries.textual_basis: 329-1.1 against 329-4.1(b); both in force on the same date.
entries.materiality: Decisive for every PT/OT determination's date-of-service and edition test, and for which incorporated document the applied bound comes from.

entries.question: On what date does the proposed edition (updated December 30, 2025, RefMed) take effect?

competing_readings.reading: Not stated; effective on publication of a Notice of Adoption
competing_readings.basis: The Regulatory Impact Statement says the effective date `will be upon publication of a Notice of Adoption in the State Register`.

The Board's assessment of public comment of 2026-08-21 anticipates adoption before the end of 2026 `with an effective date of July 2027`, and calls the January 1, 2026 date in the draft schedules a placeholder.

entries.textual_basis: Proposal text, RIS section 10, assessment of public comment (revised proposal).
entries.materiality: Without it no date-of-service clause can be decided under the proposed version: every such clause returns undetermined unless a resolution is supplied.

entries.question: How is 85 percent (and 16% under (e)(2)) of an amount that does not divide to the cent to be rounded?

competing_readings.reading: No rounding; the fraction is exact
competing_readings.basis: The text states a percentage and nothing else. The register's primitive tests exact equality.

competing_readings.reading: Rounded per the schedule's ground rules
competing_readings.basis: Fee schedules commonly carry a rounding ground rule; if this one does, the rule sits in the incorporated document.

entries.materiality: Every 85 percent or 16 percent determination whose direct amount is not a multiple of the cent-exact divisor is `not_equal` under the register and may be conforming under a rounding rule.

entries.question: Once (c)(1) and (c)(2) point PTA/OTA coding at the Acupuncture and PT/OT schedule, which document is `the fee schedule` whose RVU maximum (c)(4) preserves?

competing_readings.basis: (c)(4) is not amended by the proposal and 329-1.3 is the medical fee schedule section.
That is where the PTA/OTA codes now come from, and its ground rules carry their own daily RVU maximum.

entries.materiality: Determines which incorporated document a PT/OT daily-cap determination rests on.

entries.question: The proposal restates each amended section `to read as follows` and the restatements omit 329-1.3(e), 329-4.2(d), 333.2(c) and 348.2(c). Repeal, or drafting from a base text that lacked them?

competing_readings.basis: `is hereby amended to read as follows` followed by a full text is, read literally, the whole section.

329-1.3(e) was adopted on 2026-04-22, after the proposal was drafted; the telemedicine subdivisions were adopted in 2023 and are in the compilation; the Board's regulatory impact statement discusses residents and fellows as a focus of the update; and the revised proposal of 2026-08-21 repeats the same omissions.

entries.materiality: 27 of the 74 in-force clauses are absent from the proposed version. A determination that applies any of them and cites the proposed version has no clause to rest on.

entries.question: What Department of Health guidance makes a pre-operative COVID-19 testing protocol `required`?

competing_readings.reading: Guidance in force on the date of the test
competing_readings.basis: The subdivision is tied to a current infection and a current protocol.

competing_readings.reading: Guidance in force when the subdivision was adopted
competing_readings.basis: The text is static and names no updating mechanism.

entries.materiality: Decides whether a pre-operative test billed after the guidance changed is on a billable basis.

entries.question: Does the current medical fee schedule specify any `unit fee for a definite treatment and period of aftercare`, so that 329-1.2 has any application?

competing_readings.basis: Surgical ground rules commonly bundle aftercare into one fee.

competing_readings.reading: No; 329-1.2 is a survival from an earlier schedule
competing_readings.basis: The section was renumbered in 2015 from 329.2 and its language predates relative-value schedules.

entries.textual_basis: 329-1.2, whose applicability turns on the content of the incorporated schedule.
entries.materiality: Whether the five 329-1.2 clauses can ever arise.

waiting.$note: The second axis beside lane: what this run of the clause is waiting on. Computed at emission, per run, never stored. See _interpreter/WAITING-AXIS.md.

lanes.$note: Dispositions become data, so the router is a lookup. Named now; NOTHING READS THEM YET. The lookup is total over the dispositions in use, with an explicit no_lane state: a lane names what produces a determination, and a clause that refuses one or supplies a meaning instead has nothing to route.

clauses.text: The fee schedule applicable to medical, physical therapy and occupational therapy services shall be the medical fee schedule in effect on the date on which the medical, physical therapy or occupational therapy services were rendered, regardless of the date of accident.
clauses.assertion: The governing edition is the one in effect on the date of service, not on the date of accident.
clauses.disposition_basis: Compares the edition a determination cites against the edition this register version holds as in effect, ordered against the date of service. For physical and occupational therapy services the applicability of THIS section, against 329-4.1(b), is open: ambiguity NY-A1.

then.value: NY-A1 unresolved: whether 329-1.1 or 329-4.1(b) governs a physical or occupational therapy service is open, and nobody has settled it.

evaluate.$applicability_needs_resolution: Whether this section applies to a PT/OT service at all IS the open question NY-A1; the applicability gate must sit under the guard on that resolution.

clauses.text: When the schedule specifies a unit fee for a definite treatment and period of aftercare, and the patient is transferred from one to another physician, the employer (or carrier) is responsible for the amount stated in the schedule.
clauses.assertion: On transfer under a unit fee the employer owes the scheduled amount, once.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where a unit fee is specified and a transfer occurred. The scheduled amount is licensed text; the determination supplies it as the applied bound and the register tests the total paid against it.

note.value: equal: the employer paid the scheduled unit fee once across the concerned physicians. The unit fee itself is licensed content supplied on the determination.

clauses.text: If the concerned physicians agree upon amount of proration, they shall render separate bills accordingly;
clauses.assertion: Agreed proration is billed separately.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only on an agreement.

clauses.text: in the event of no agreement, the matter shall be settled by by an arbitration committee appointed pursuant to section 13-g of the Workers' Compensation Law without cost to the contestants.
clauses.assertion: Disagreement is settled by a 13-g arbitration committee.
clauses.disposition_basis: Directs a referral. No fact of a bill makes it true or false. The doubled `by by` is the compilation's text and is kept.

clauses.text: When treatment is terminated by death before the expiration of the allowable period of aftercare, the appropriate fee shall apply without proration.
clauses.assertion: Death before aftercare ends leaves the full scheduled fee payable.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only on termination by death.

note.value: satisfied: the full scheduled fee was paid without proration.

clauses.text: When treatment is terminated by departure of the injured worker from New York State before the expiration of the allowable period of aftercare, the fee shall be the earned portion of the appropriate fee, having regard for the fact that generally the greater portion is earned at the time of operation or other procedure.
clauses.assertion: On departure the fee is the earned portion.
clauses.disposition_basis: `earned portion` and `having regard for` name a standard and no test.

note.value: affirmed: the fee paid is the earned portion, as assessed. Never inferred.

clauses.text: The medical fee schedule for medical services shall be the Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule, updated December 30, 2025, prepared by the board and published by RefMed, which is herein incorporated by reference.
clauses.assertion: Identifies the edition of the medical fee schedule that is the fee schedule.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the edition identity (update date, publisher) that the date-of-service clauses test a cited edition against. It decides nothing itself.
clauses.operative_weight: Edition identity: updated 2025-12-30, publisher RefMed, effective date NOT STATED (NY-A2).

clauses.text: [the fee amounts, relative value units, conversion factors and ground rules of the Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule, incorporated by reference and not reproduced]
clauses.assertion: The operative fee rules are stated in the incorporated schedule.
clauses.disposition_basis: The rule a determination applies when it applies a scheduled amount is stated in a document this register does not hold and which 329-1.3(b) says may be purchased. Distinct from undetermined: the register knows where the rule is.

incorporated_document.document: Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule
incorporated_document.retrieval: purchase, per 329-1.3(b); examination at the Department of State and listed libraries

clauses.text: The Official New York Workers' Compensation Medical Fee Schedule incorporated by reference herein may be examined at the office of the Department of State, One Commerce Plaza, 99 Washington Avenue, Albany, NY 12231, the Legislative Library, the libraries of the New York State Supreme Court, and the district offices of the board. Copies may be purchased from RefMed by telephone at (863) 222-4071 or online at https://marketplace.refmed.com, keyword New York.
clauses.assertion: The incorporated schedule may be examined at listed public offices and purchased from the publisher.
clauses.disposition_basis: Supplies the retrieval condition the INCORPORATED_BY_REFERENCE clauses record: examination or purchase.
clauses.operative_weight: Retrieval condition of the incorporated document: examination at listed offices, or purchase from RefMed.

clauses.text: Physical Therapy Assistants (PTAs) and Occupational Therapy Assistants (OTAs) may provide services under the direct supervision of an authorized Physical Therapist (PT) or authorized Occupational Therapist (OT) respectively.
clauses.assertion: A PTA or OTA service is permitted only under direct supervision of an authorized PT or OT of the matching discipline.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where the rendering provider is a PTA or OTA.

clauses.text: When billing for PTA services, supervising authorized PTs must select codes from the Official New York State Acupuncture and Physical and Occupational Therapy Fee Schedule incorporated by reference in Section 329-4.2 of Title 12 NYCRR that are permissible and within the scope of practice for PTAs using modifier CQ.
clauses.assertion: PTA services are coded from a named schedule section.
clauses.disposition_basis: Which schedule the codes come from is recorded on the determination; the register compares it against the section this version names. THE NAMED SOURCE CHANGES BETWEEN VERSIONS: the Physical Medicine Section of the Medical Fee Schedule in force, the Acupuncture and PT/OT schedule under 329-4.2 as proposed.

clauses.text: [PTA services are billed] using modifier CQ.
clauses.assertion: A PTA service carries modifier CQ.
clauses.disposition_basis: Membership of a modifier in the bill's modifier list.

clauses.text: When billing for OTA services, supervising authorized OTs must select codes from the Official New York State Workers' Compensation Acupuncture and Physical and Occupational Therapy Fee Schedule incorporated by reference in Section 329-4.2 of Title 12 NYCRR that are permissible and within the scope of practice of OTAs using modifier CO.
clauses.assertion: OTA services are coded from a named schedule section.
clauses.disposition_basis: As (c)(1), for OTAs. The named source changes between versions.

clauses.text: [OTA services are billed] using modifier CO.
clauses.assertion: An OTA service carries modifier CO.
clauses.disposition_basis: Membership of a modifier in the bill's modifier list.

clauses.text: Services billed using the modifiers CQ or CO must be billed and paid at 85 percent of the amount payable for such services had they been performed directly by PTs and OTs.
clauses.assertion: A CQ or CO service is paid at exactly 85 percent of the direct-therapist amount.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where CQ or CO is billed. The direct-therapist amount is licensed schedule content and arrives as a supplied bound; the register tests the fraction. No rounding convention is stated: NY-A5.

note.value: Exact: 100 x paid == 85 x the direct-therapist amount at a common scale. No rounding convention is stated (NY-A5).

clauses.text: Clinical notes by PTAs must be cosigned by the supervising PT. Clinical notes by OTAs must be cosigned by the supervising OT.
clauses.assertion: Assistant notes are cosigned by the supervising therapist of the same discipline.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only for a PTA or OTA service.

clauses.text: PTAs and OTAs may not provide services or bill for services independently.
clauses.assertion: The billing provider for a PTA or OTA service is never the assistant.
clauses.disposition_basis: Class of the billing provider against the assistant classes.

clauses.text: Nothing in this section shall change the maximum numbers of billable Relative Value Units (RVUs) for physical therapy and occupational therapy on any given date of service, as outlined elsewhere in the fee schedule. They are not increased or otherwise changed based on whether the services are provided by PTs, OTs, PTAs or OTAs.
clauses.assertion: The daily RVU maximum is the schedule's and is unchanged by assistant provision.
clauses.disposition_basis: The maximum itself is `outlined elsewhere in the fee schedule`, which is the incorporated document. The register records that the cap applies unchanged and does not hold its value. Under the proposed version `the fee schedule` for PTA/OTA codes is the Acupuncture and PT/OT schedule: NY-A6.

incorporated_document.document: the fee schedule incorporated by 329-1.3(a) (in force) or, for PTA/OTA codes, the schedule named by 329-1.3(c)(1) and (2) as proposed

clauses.text: When services are performed by PTs and PTAs (or OTs and OTAs) on the same date of service, the services applied to the maximum number of RVUs on any given date of service shall be determined giving priority to services provided by PTs over those provided by PTAs, and services provided by OTs over those provided by OTAs.
clauses.assertion: On a mixed day, therapist services are applied to the cap before assistant services.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only on a same-day mix. The determination records which class was given priority; the cap value itself is incorporated (c)(4).

clauses.text: The ability of PTAs and OTAs to provide services under NYS Workers Compensation, and for supervising PTs and OTs to submit bills for said services, shall in no way expand or otherwise change the scope of practice or permissible activities for PTAs or OTAs by statute, and/or any applicable regulations promulgated by the New York State Education Department, New York State Department of Health, or the New York State Workers' Compensation Board. As such, it shall be impermissible for PTAs/OTAs to perform any services or activities otherwise reserved for PTs and OTs respectively, or for supervising PTs or OTs to bill for such services, and Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes must be selected accordingly.
clauses.assertion: A service reserved to PTs or OTs by statute or regulation is impermissible for an assistant and may not be billed.
clauses.disposition_basis: Whether a service is `otherwise reserved` is decided by external statute and regulation the register does not hold; it arrives as a held assessment.

note.value: affirmed: the service IS reserved to PTs or OTs, so the assistant provision and its billing are impermissible. The reservation is decided under external statute and regulation; it arrives as an assessment.

clauses.text: Examples may include, but are not limited to: a PTA is prohibited by section 6738(a) of the NYS Education Law from performing evaluation, testing, interpretation, planning or modification of patient/client programs; a PT conducts the initial evaluation and develops the plan of care, and the treatment may be provided by the PTA; PTAs and OTAs may not perform Functional Capacity Evaluations (FCEs).
clauses.assertion: Examples of reserved services.
clauses.disposition_basis: `Examples may include, but are not limited to`. It bounds (c)(6) by instance and tests nothing; the schema names ILLUSTRATIVE as not a category, and this clause is its second instance in the estate.

clauses.text: When workers' compensation benefits are sought due to a workplace exposure to COVID-19, reimbursement for serological, molecular or other reliable testing to confirm a current COVID-19 viral infection may be made using CPT code 87635.
clauses.assertion: Confirmatory COVID-19 testing on a workplace-exposure claim is billed under code 87635.
clauses.disposition_basis: Arises only where a test is billed on a workplace-exposure claim. The code is cited by identifier; its descriptor is not reproduced.

clauses.text: The RVU for CPT code 87635 shall be 39.18,
clauses.assertion: The relative value unit for 87635 is 39.18.
clauses.disposition_basis: A number stated in the regulation itself, so the register holds it and tests the determination's applied RVU against it.

clauses.text: and the total fee for such test shall be 51.33 for Region IV, 47.41 for Region III, and 41.53 for Regions I and II.
clauses.assertion: The fee for 87635 is fixed by region.
clauses.disposition_basis: Amounts stated in the regulation itself, selected by region. This is the one bound in the register that a party holding zero schedule text can verify to the cent.

note.value: The three fees are the regulation's own numbers (51.33 / 47.41 / 41.53 USD), the one bound in this register a party holding no schedule text can verify to the cent.

clauses.text: CPT code 87635 may only be billed when there is a claim for workers' compensation due to a COVID-19 infection as a result of a workplace exposure or when testing for COVID-19 is administered as part of a required pre-operative testing protocol in accordance with Department of Health guidance.
clauses.assertion: 87635 is billable on exactly two bases.
clauses.disposition_basis: Membership of the recorded claim basis in a closed two-value set.

clauses.text: CPT code 87635 may not be billed for routine screening of workers' compensation claimants for the presence of the COVID-19 virus.
clauses.assertion: Routine screening is not a billable basis.
clauses.disposition_basis: The recorded basis against one prohibited value.

clauses.text: Antibody testing is not available under the Official New York Workers' Compensation Fee Schedule.
clauses.assertion: No antibody test is payable.
clauses.disposition_basis: A prohibited class against the tests billed.
